belief: Forgiving means pretending it didn’t hurt.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that forgiving means pretending it didn’t hurt, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Being told to “just get over it” when you were hurt. Family rules that said not to talk about painful things. Pressure to look peaceful and spiritual. Fear that admitting pain means you are bitter. Seeing forgiveness only as a quick, cheerful act instead of an honest process.
teaches: Real forgiveness starts by honestly naming the wrong. Joseph told his brothers plainly that they had intended evil against him, and then he forgave them. David poured out the pain of betrayal by a close friend. God keeps track of your tears. Even Jesus, as He forgave from the cross, did not pretend the cross was not happening. Forgiveness does not deny the hurt; it chooses to release the debt to God while still feeling the loss.
self_statements: If I’ve forgiven, I shouldn’t still hurt.
Talking about the pain means I’m bitter.
I have to act like it was no big deal.
Christians should get over things quickly.
Admitting it hurt would make me unforgiving.
If I still feel sad, I haven’t really forgiven.
errors: Believing you must either feel no pain or not have forgiven.
Pretending a real wound is not there.
“I should be over this by now.”
Thinking forgiveness is a feeling rather than a decision.
questions: Did Joseph pretend his brothers had not hurt him?
What did David do with the pain of betrayal?
What does it mean that God keeps my tears in His bottle?
Is forgiveness a feeling or a choice to release a debt?
Can I still feel sad and have forgiven?
Who taught me that admitting pain is unforgiving?
What would honest forgiveness look like for me?
truth: Forgiving does not mean pretending it didn’t hurt. I can name the wrong honestly, feel the pain, and still choose to release the debt to God. God sees my tears and cares about my wounds. Forgiveness is a choice I may need to make again and again as the hurt heals.
hw_questions: Did Joseph pretend he wasn’t hurt?
What did David do with betrayal?
What does God do with my tears?
Is forgiveness a feeling or a choice?
Can I still feel sad and have forgiven?
What would honest forgiveness look like?
hw_truths: I can name the hurt honestly and still forgive.
God sees and keeps my tears.
Forgiveness is a choice, not a feeling.
I can release the debt and still grieve the loss.
I can entrust the one who hurt me to God, who judges justly.
Healing takes time, and that is okay.
log: Each day, write what still hurts, then write a short prayer releasing the debt to God again.
name_example: As for you, what you intended against Sarah for evil, God intended for good.
actions: Write down exactly what happened and how it hurt you,
then write, “I choose to release this debt to God.”
and notice how Joseph named the wrong and still forgave.
Share the hurt with one safe person
without having to wrap it up neatly.
“It still hurts, and I still choose to forgive.”
tracker: One time I chose to forgive again
prayer: Father, thank You that You see my tears and care about my wounds. Help me reject the lie that forgiving means pretending it didn’t hurt. Help me be honest about the pain, release the debt to You, and trust You with justice. Heal my heart in Your time. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
